subject: Post-call: CsUnity dedicated capacity — guardrails, isolation & scaling
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@csunity.ai>, Procurement <procurement@csunity.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity guardrails, isolation & scaling

Alex / CsUnity team — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared record. Please reply with corrections or missing items.

Key pain points you described:
- Unpredictable tail latency during morning and evening traffic spikes (p95 currently ~420ms).
- Strict tenant data isolation: model state and KV cache cannot be shared across tenants.
- Procurement requires predictable committed spend and an SLA for business-critical inference.
- Regulatory requirement to control egress and have customer-managed KMS for keys.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Stable p95 inference latency <= 150ms for the 7B and 13B models at target QPS.
- Dedicated capacity that guarantees tenant isolation (no cross-tenant KV sharing).
- Autoscale path to support bursts up to ~3x baseline within 10 minutes.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool with escalation contacts and 15 min paging for major incidents.

Initial sizing & configuration we discussed:
- Start: reserved pool equivalent to 8 x A100-class GPUs (supports baseline throughput for 7B/13B in quantized and fp16 paths).
- Burst target: scale up to 24 GPUs via reserved-burst capacity or short-term capacity reservations.
- Isolation: tenant-dedicated pools with separate KV namespaces and per-tenant model endpoints.
- Network/security: VPC peering, allowlist IP ranges, and customer KMS integration for model artifacts and logs.

Risk & mitigations:
- Cost during sustained burst: recommend a fallback policy that routes low-priority traffic to a smaller quantized 7B variant.
- Cold-cache latency for large context windows: we recommend prefix caching and a pre-warm canary for known heavy tenants.

Attachments included for reference:
- capacity-estimate-csunity.pdf (breakdown of GPU sizing, cost bands, and estimated token throughput)
- network-topology-diagram.png (proposed VPC layout and peering)
- draft-ma-term-sheet.docx (commercial draft for procurement to review)

Next steps (owner — ETA):
- Rachel: Send written SOW + sizing worksheet by Wed 5/29.
- Jordan: Draft ops playbook (canary rollout + autoscale policy) by Fri 6/4.
- Neha: Security checklist + KMS integration notes by Tue 6/1.
- Alex / Procurement: Share preferred commercial terms and PO cadence by Mon 6/7.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute working session next Tuesday 6/1 to walk the SOW and network diagram. I’ll send a calendar invite if that works for you.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — this is a helpful summary and matches our notes. A few clarifications from procurement side: 
- Target contract start: July 15 (would like a 12-month committed term with quarterly true-ups).
- Can you provide a pricing band for 8GPU baseline and 24GPU burst (separate lines for committed rate vs burst uplift)?

On tech: the 150ms p95 target is what our product team wants; we'd accept a phased SLO if you can show a canary plan to reach it within Q1 post-go-live.

I'll introduce Maria Gomez from procurement on the next thread — Maria, copied here.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity guardrails, isolation & scaling (internal)

Internal notes / ops suggestions based on the call: 
- Propose a staged canary: 1 tenant on isolated pool (2 GPUs) -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full. Include KV prewarm script to avoid heavy cold-cache tails.
- Autoscale policy: fixed step scaling (8 -> 12 -> 16 -> 24) with cooldown 3m; prioritize burst via reserved-burst tokens to avoid paying on-demand when possible.
- Fallback: implement automatic downgrade to 7B-quantized for non-critical traffic after 250ms queueing time. This will reduce cost and free capacity for critical requests.
- Ops runbook: include contact matrix (15m P1 paging), postmortem template, and a metric dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latencies, token/sec, active sessions, cache hit rate.

I'll draft the ops playbook and share by Friday. Rachel — for the SOW, suggest we add a paragraph on data separation verifying there is zero KV namespace sharing and how we validate it during onboarding.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
